intro: A fairly quiet day. The big themes: AI agents getting let through websites' bot checks, creators pushing back on Instagram's Amazon links, and retailers' ad businesses growing faster than their shops.

must_reads.title: Google tells websites how to wave its AI agent past bot checks
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Google is asking sites to let its shopping/browsing agent past bot checks. When an agent, not a person, clicks a link, redirects and tracking have to work for it too, or the click and the commission can be lost.

must_reads.title: Some creators are skeptical of Instagram’s new affiliate program
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Creators worry the new Instagram Amazon links pay little and favour one store. That tension shows creators still want links that work across stores and platforms, not just the one a platform picks.

must_reads.title: Walmart and Target's ad businesses outpace online sales as AI reshapes shopping
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Walmart and Target now grow ads faster than online sales, and Target's AI assistant shoppers buy at about twice the usual rate. Retailers are putting money into their own media and AI, which can shift what they pay creators and affiliates.

must_reads.title: Levanta adds TikTok Shop creator affiliate management
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Levanta, which works on Amazon creator and brand attribution, now also manages TikTok Shop affiliates. Attribution tools are spreading across platforms, the same cross-platform space Geniuslink plays in.

must_reads.title: Creator spend forecast at $116bn, affiliate commissions included
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: A new forecast puts creator spending at $116bn, counting affiliate commissions. Affiliate is being counted as part of the creator budget, a sign the two markets are merging.
